fieldReports: I-Trekkings reported reverse Tarraluoppal-Sammarlappa in 3 hours 45 minutes on 2006-08-02.

Field reports note wet planks, stony lower trail, mosquitoes, and weather as practical speed factors.

difficulty.label: moderate remote valley stage; mostly easy walking with wet/stony sections
officialClaims: STF gives 15 km and 4-6 hours but no formal difficulty grade.
Naturkartan describes mostly easy-walked mountain moor, planked wetlands, small hills, wet marshes, birch forest, and Slihtajåhkå suspension bridge.
Laponia describes Badjelánndaleden generally as easy and says there are no difficult fords.
keyHazards: Wet and boardwalked ground near Darreluoppal and on the approach to Såmmarlappa.
Small waterways and mapped fords in the first half can vary with snowmelt and rain.
Slihtajåhkå suspension bridge currentness should be checked before publication.
Stony/boggy lower sections, slick planks, mosquitoes, poor visibility, and remoteness.
The route crosses/skirts Sarek, Padjelanta/Badjelánnda, and Pärlälvens fjällurskog contexts, so rules and current closures are nuanced.

rules.rule: In Laponia national parks, dogs are prohibited except leashed dogs from 1 January to 30 April, with specific exceptions not covering normal Padjelantaleden summer hiking.

Drone flights, low flights, and aircraft start/landing in Padjelanta/Badjelánnda, Sarek, and Stora Sjöfallet/Stuor Muorkke require County Administrative Board permission outside official/Sámi-right exceptions.
Do not disturb reindeer or herding work; wait or detour around animals, avoid splitting herds, and do not camp beside enclosures.

In national parks, hunting/fishing are generally prohibited except designated Padjelanta fishing waters with valid permit. Pärlälvens reserve portions allow hunting/fishing only under applicable law and permits. Exact water-specific checks are needed before importing any fishing context.
